title: Surjectivity detected modulo a Jacobson ideal
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, I an ideal such that every 1+x with x in I is a unit, M an R-module, N a finitely generated R-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and f : M → N an R-linear map. If (R/I) ⊗_R f is surjective, then f is surjective.

source.place: Tag 00DV, Nakayama, applied in the proof of Tag 0BCB

proof.text: For x in I and y in R, 1+xy is a unit by hypothesis, so Ideal.mem_jacobson_bot places I in the Jacobson radical. Use TensorProduct.quotTensorEquivQuotSMul to identify reduction with the quotient by I times the module. The quotient maps are surjective; the tensor map surjectivity gives surjectivity of M → N/IN.

source.place: Tag 00DV, Nakayama, applied in the proof of Tag 0BCB

proof.text: Apply Nakayama to N/range(f), which is finite and has zero reduction. In Lean this is the range formulation LinearMap.surjective_of_surjective_comp_mkQ. It gives surjectivity of f.

lean.statement:
theorem surjective_of_extendScalars_mod_ideal {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    (I : Ideal R) (hunits : ∀ x : I, IsUnit (1 + (x : R)))
    (M N : ModuleCat.{max u v} R) [Module.Finite R N] (f : M ⟶ N)
    (hf : Function.Surjective ((ModuleCat.extendScalars (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).map f)) :
    Function.Surjective f
